name: Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle designed to travel on no more than three wheels, other than a motor-driven cycle, motor-assisted bicycle or electric bicycle; an electric two-wheeler whose motor exceeds two brake horsepower (1,500 W) or that can go faster than 30 mph is one.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground; includes autocycles
Anything faster or more powerful than a motor-driven cycle (two brake horsepower, 30 mph) is a motorcycle
Riders need a driver's or junior driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement, earned by passing a knowledge exam and a skills exam
Every rider and passenger must wear a helmet meeting FMVSS 218 on a highway, except in a fully enclosed autocycle
The operator must wear glasses, goggles or a face shield if it has no windshield
Registered with the DMV each year, and must carry liability insurance
An off-road motorcycle must pass a Vermont state safety inspection before it can be registered or titled for road use
Off the highway, a two-wheeled vehicle is an ATV, with its registration and trail-decal rules, only if it has permanent, full-time power to both wheels; an ordinary electric dirt bike isn't one
Ridden in the travel lanes like any motor vehicle
